Outsiders generally believe that Apple CEO Tim Cook's remarks during this earnings call were vague, seemingly implying that the more heavily Siri's AI features are used, the higher the costs incurred may be compared to our current expectations.

Although it has long been understood by the outside world that unlimited use of Siri's AI features inevitably comes at some price, Cook's remarks do indeed seem to foreshadow some disappointing news…

What we know so far

Apple has always wanted to run AI computation on-device as much as possible, achieving two goals at once: maximising user privacy while also sparing Apple the server costs required to handle these tasks. However, some work still relies on Apple's own Private Cloud Compute servers, and some even requires the use of Google's Gemini servers.

Server usage naturally involves expenses, so the outside world has always tacitly assumed that Apple would follow the practice of other companies and adopt a freemium business model for Siri AI: a free tier with usage limits, with heavy users required to pay for a subscription.

However, the prevailing understanding so far is that to use Siri's AI features, one only needs to subscribe to iCloud+; some have speculated that the usage cap may be tied to the iCloud+ plan—50GB corresponding to a certain limit, 200GB to a higher limit, and 2TB to an even higher limit.

In other words, many of us may be able to enjoy a higher Siri AI usage allowance as part of our existing iCloud+ plan.

But we may have to pay extra

On this earnings call, Goldman Sachs put a question to Cook on this matter.

Cook's response seemed to suggest more than merely pointing out that an iCloud+ subscription is required:

Some interpret this as meaning that a higher Siri AI usage allowance is not something one can simply enjoy by subscribing to iCloud+, but must be purchased additionally. In other words, the subscription itself does not automatically bring a higher usage cap—it only gives you the option to purchase an upgraded allowance.

Given the ambiguous wording, the above may not be what was intended. However, if what Cook truly meant to convey was simply that "a higher usage cap is included in the iCloud+ subscription," one would expect him to have said so more clearly and explicitly. It is precisely this vagueness that leads one to suspect the news may not be good—or, at the very least, to take him at his word and believe that Apple has not yet made a final decision but is considering the direction of "additional paid purchases."

Of course, it is still too early to say; it will depend on how frequently we actually use Siri AI and when we might hit the usage cap. Even if my speculation proves correct, it may not affect the majority of Apple users. Nevertheless, based on the experience with current AI chatbots, many people who find them genuinely useful beyond occasional tasks often end up having to pay for a subscription.

What are your thoughts? Do you agree with my reading of Cook's subtext? If so, do you think you would be willing to pay to use Siri's AI features? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
